svg.text: WAF tier topology options (within end-to-end application delivery)
Initial focus is the F5 WAF tier; mini-diagrams show one site per option (4-tenant / 2-site LTM + WAF counts noted). LTM = Local Traffic Manager; DSC = HA Cluster.
Per Tenant / Per Site: W1-3 (3 WAFs, N-2) vs. W1-2 sub-variant (2 WAFs)
W1-2 drops WAF 3 → 50% tenant cap loss / 0 N-2
W1-3: 16 LTM + 24 WAF = 40 | W1-2 sub-variant: 16 LTM + 16 WAF = 32
W1-3 passes ≤25% cap + N-2; W1-2 needs X2A for 99.95% maintenance + 2nd fault.
W2 — Dedicated LTM + WAF HA Cluster (DSC)
Per Tenant / Per Site (2-node Active/Standby WAF cluster)
4 tenants / 2 sites: 16 LTM + 16 WAF = 32 (W2b; or 0+16 if no LTM)
Simple pair boundary, but zero local redundancy left during maintenance of 1 node.
Priority Group 1: Dedicated WAFs | Priority Group 2: Shared Reserve
4 tenants / 2 sites: 16 LTM + 20 WAF = 36 (16 pref + 4 reserve)
Dedicated normal path; saves only 4 WAFs vs W1-3 while adding reserve contention.
W4 — Asymmetric Site 1 Cluster + Extra WAF
4 tenants / 2 sites: 16 LTM + 20 WAF = 36 (3/tenant S1 + 2/tenant S2)
Extra Site 1 resilience, but DR site (Site 2) has weaker maintenance/failure headroom.
S1 / S1+2 — Tenant LTMs + Shared WAFs
4 Tenant LTM HA Pairs → Shared Active Pool (S1: 4/site | S1+2: 4 + 2 = 6/site)
+2 absorbs rolling upgrades, SSD outage & canary; needs strict policy gates for ≤25%.
S2 — Shared LTM + Shared WAF Pool
All 4 Tenants Share Both the LTM Tier and the WAF Pool
4 tenants / 2 sites: 4 LTM + 8 WAF = 12 (fails ≤25% impact cap)
Breaks tenant LTM isolation; one bad change affects 100% (all 4 tenants) at once.
Confirmed Target Hardware Standard: F5 rSeries r2800 Pizza Boxes ONLY (F5OS-A 1.8.0+ • No Blade Chassis)
• Both W1-3 (2-tenant F5OS @ 4c/12G) AND S1+2 (full-box @ 8c/24G) land at 20 r2800s total (8 LTM @ 2/box + 12 WAF) — benchmark AWAF RAM in Phase 0.
• Guardrails: single 480 GB SSD (no RAID-1 → remote HSL logs + K+2 spread + cloud-init rebuild) • no STP on r2800 (dual-homed LACP LAGs, K000152319).
